Ya están todas las piezas: [[ia-tokens|t: All the pieces are now in place: [[ia-tokens|cutting the text into pieces]], [[ia-secuencias|predicting the next piece]], [[ia-vectores-palabras|representing words as vectors]] and [[ia-atencion|attention]]. This topic puts them together into a single thing that is trained right here, and then looks honestly at what changes when that is multiplied by a thousand million. From [[al-radicales-log|logarithms]] comes the way of reading those graphs.
Un modelo de lenguaje grande no tiene ni: A large language model has no piece you have not already seen. It is a [[ia-atencion|transformer]] stacked many times, trained with [[av-informacion|cross entropy]] to predict the next token. Everything else —what looks like magic— comes from repeating that with very many more numbers and very much more text.
El entrenamiento base tiene un objetivo: The base training has a one-line objective: given a piece of text, get the next token right. Real text is taken, cut anywhere, and the model is asked for the probability of what came afterwards. The loss is the same old cross entropy.
Es exactamente [[ia-secuencias|la misma:
It is exactly [[ia-secuencias|the same formula]] that scored an n-gram model, with two differences: the context is not the last $n$ symbols but everything before, up to the window's limit, and the probability does not come from counting but from a network.

The notable thing is that the label is the text itself. Nobody needs to annotate anything: any text serves as an example of itself, and that is why it could be trained with amounts of data no hand-labelled task would have allowed.
Un transformador diminuto —una capa de a: A tiny transformer —one causal attention layer, one dense network, normalisation and residual connections— on a 373-letter text, in Spanish. Train it and ask it to write. It is the same engine you have used throughout the block.
Con unos cuatro mil números que ajustar: With some four thousand numbers to adjust and fewer than a thousand letters of text, what do you expect it to write: correct Spanish, recognisable individual words, or noise?

El modelo no ve todo el texto del mundo: The model does not see all the world's text at once: it sees a window of so many tokens. What is left outside simply does not exist for it at that moment. And enlarging the window is not free, from what you already know about [[ia-atencion|attention]]: each token is compared with all the others, so the cost grows with the square of the length.

Leyes de escala, y cómo se leen: Scaling laws, and how they are read
Al entrenar modelos de tamaños muy disti: On training models of very different sizes something regular was observed: the loss falls following approximately a power law with respect to the number of parameters, the amount of text and the computation used. What is interesting for us is what shape that has, because it is pure [[al-radicales-log|logarithm]] mathematics.

Tomando logaritmos a los dos lados, una:
Taking logarithms on both sides, a power becomes a straight line: the slope is $-\alpha$ and the intercept is $\log c$.

That is why these graphs are always drawn with both axes logarithmic: if the points fall in a straight line, there is a power law, and the slope measures the exponent. It is the same trick used to detect power laws anywhere else.

Conviene decir qué <em>no</em> demuestra: It is worth saying what this page does not prove. Training the model above at several sizes, the loss does not fall in a straight line: with this text and this training budget, the best result comes with about 4000 numbers, and from there on growing makes it worse. That does not refute the scaling laws; it says that they cannot be measured here. To see them you have to grow the model, the text and the computation at the same time, and adjust the learning rate at each size; with fewer than four hundred letters and a few thousand steps, what dominates the result is the budget, not the size. Be suspicious of a line fitted to five noisy points, here and anywhere else.
Un modelo recién preentrenado sabe conti: A freshly pretrained model knows how to continue text, and nothing more. If you write it a question, the statistically most likely thing may be another similar question, because on the internet questions usually come in lists. For it to answer you have to ask it another way.
<strong>Ajuste con ejemplos.</strong> Se: Fine-tuning with examples. Training continues with the same loss, but on well-written instruction and answer pairs. It is the same pretraining on more select text.
<strong>Ajuste por preferencias.</strong: Fine-tuning by preferences. A person is shown two answers and asked which they prefer. With those comparisons something that scores answers is trained, and afterwards the model is adjusted to raise that score.
Ese segundo paso es donde entra [[ia-ref: That second step is where [[ia-refuerzo|reinforcement learning]] comes in, and also where [[ia-limites|Goodhart's law]] appears: as soon as the score becomes the objective, the model learns to raise it by routes nobody wanted —long answers that look complete, feigned confidence, speaking prettily without saying anything—. Optimising the measure spoils the measure.
Y aquí empieza el problema siguiente: And here the next problem begins
Conviene tener clara una consecuencia de: It is worth being clear about one consequence of all the above. The objective, from beginning to end, is producing probable text. Nowhere in the loss is there a term measuring whether what is said is true. That it gets it right so often is because in the text it was trained on the true thing was, almost always, the most frequent; and that it invents with aplomb is because an invented statement with the right form is also probable text.

That it gets so much right is because in the training text the true thing is usually the most frequent, not because there is a truthfulness check somewhere.

Puede influir, pero no explica la seguri: It may have an influence, but it does not explain the confidence with which it says it. Even if the fact were there a thousand times, the objective would still be the text's probability and not its truthfulness.
Saber que el objetivo es la probabilidad: Knowing that the objective is the next token's probability explains almost everything that is disconcerting when using them. It explains their inventing references with impeccable formatting, the same question put in two ways giving different answers, their being better at what abounds on the internet than at what is scarce, and asking them to “think step by step” working: writing the intermediate steps makes each next token easier to get right. None of that is mysterious once you know what is being minimised.
El camino es corto y está bien documenta: The path is short and well documented. The transformer is from 2017. In 2018 it was seen that pretraining on unlabelled text and fine-tuning afterwards for each task worked far better than training each task separately. From there, the discovery with the most consequences was not an idea but an empirical observation: that the same recipes kept improving as they were enlarged, with no sign of running out, and that at a certain scale capabilities appeared that had not been sought. Much of what has happened since then is a consequence of taking that observation seriously.
